notes: Metallus is the public specialty steel maker (NYSE: MTUS) formerly named TimkenSteel; its 10-K for the year ended Dec. 31, 2024 reports about 1,880 employees, an Ohio state of incorporation and headquarters at 1835 Dueber Avenue SW in Canton. The EIN on the 990 matches the EIN in the 10-K exactly. JobsOhio's July 2024 report lists a $3.0 million Economic Development Grant and a $500,000 Workforce Grant for a $112.7 million Stark County project with 1,602 jobs retained; the company was created in Ohio in 2014 as a spinoff of Canton-based Timken.

parent: Miami University (State of Ohio public university)
notes: The $1.5 million is a JobsOhio Vibrant Community Grant for the Lee and Rosemary Fisher Innovation College@Elm, a 39,000-square-foot incubator in Oxford built with the City of Oxford and The Fischer Group. The Ohio Department of Development's Major Employers report ranks Miami University 73rd in the state with 4,442 Ohio employees; the university was founded in Oxford in 1809.

Cenovus Energy's 2024 Annual Information Form, filed with its Form 40-F, lists Husky Marketing and Supply Company as a wholly owned Delaware material subsidiary and reports 7,150 full-time-equivalent employees at Dec. 31, 2024; Cenovus is headquartered in Calgary, Alberta. The Dublin, Ohio address is the US regional office; JobsOhio's July 2024 report shows a $4.0 million Workforce Grant against a $1.44 billion investment at the Lima and Toledo refineries, with 942 jobs retained.

MedShip is an operating distributor of surgical dressings, not a developer: the $750,000 Vibrant Community Grant paid for its own 12,000-square-foot headquarters in downtown Camden, which it built after demolishing two blighted buildings and into which it invested $2.3 million of its own money. Its COO says 86 of the company's 93 employees work in Camden, and JobsOhio calls MedShip an Ohio-grown startup less than four years old.

Not a project LLC: King's Command Foods (2022), LLC runs a federally inspected prepared-foods plant at 770 N. Center St. in Versailles, and the $425,000 Economic Development Grant backed a $20.4 million expansion of that plant with 150 jobs retained and 60 created, so it is classed as a business. The Sidney Daily News reported in 2016 that the cooking operations are based in Kent, Washington, with another plant in Oklahoma City, and that the business had combined with American Prepared Foods Group of Green Bay, Wisconsin. I could not confirm who owns it after the 2022 change the entity name implies, and no worldwide employee figure was found, so the bucket is an inference from the three-plant footprint; graded D.

EPC is an injection molder founded in 1994 by Reza Kargarzadeh, who still owns and runs it; the JobsOhio release describes more than 14 facilities in ten states and Mexico, over 200 molding machines, and 200-plus employees at one plant alone, which is why the bucket is 500-4999 rather than a counted figure. The 990 address is Grinnell, Iowa; JobsOhio's January 2025 report shows a $350,000 Economic Development Grant for a $9 million Huron County project with 180 jobs retained.

Battle Motors builds refuse and vocational trucks at the former Crane Carrier plant in New Philadelphia, which Wikipedia records it bought in 2021 and which Crane Carrier's founder Robert Zeligson started in 1946. JobsOhio's February 2025 report lists 591 jobs retained and 309 created in Tuscarawas County against a $21.9 million investment, so the Ohio site alone is over 500; the company reported layoffs in New Philadelphia in early 2025, so the figure may have fallen.

This is a spec-building grant, not a company expansion: the $360,000 came through the Ohio Site Inventory Program for a 30,000-square-foot speculative industrial and office building in the Salt Creek Industrial Park in Jackson County, built to attract tenants that have not been named. JobsOhio's own report lists the jobs, industry and investment as TBD. No separate developer or employee count was named, so the LLC is treated as its own parent.

Haag-Streit's own site says the Haag-Streit Group was integrated into Metall Zug AG as its medical devices business unit in 2018, and Metall Zug's site says the holding company is based in Zug, Switzerland and employs about 900 people worldwide. Haag-Streit USA in Mason is the group's US sales and service arm; JobsOhio's August 2024 report shows a $200,000 Economic Development Grant for a $4.9 million Warren County project with 114 jobs retained.

Classed as a business rather than site development because warehousing is what Pinnacle sells: OhioSE describes it and its affiliate Trinity Real Estate USA, LLC, both run by president John Jack, as providing warehousing, repackaging and transportation from an ISO-certified plant. The $160,000 Revitalization Grant paid to bring the former Mahle Engine building in Caldwell, vacant since 2009, back into use for Pinnacle's own operations; JobsOhio lists 21 jobs retained and 13 created.

Safecor Health repackages unit-dose drugs for more than 1,000 hospitals and has had its headquarters in Columbus since 2011, though it was founded in 2008; the $150,000 Workforce Grant supported a Franklin County expansion with 129 jobs retained and 100 created. Google News indexes a PR Newswire release on an August 2021 recapitalization by Vesey Street Capital Partners, a New York health-care private-equity firm; under the method the operating company, not the fund, is the parent.

JobsOhio calls Mira an Ohio-based, privately held precision-medicine company founded in 2020 that runs molecular diagnostic testing through independent pharmacies and primary-care practices, and the grant tripled the size of its Mason lab. The July 2024 report shows a $100,000 Economic Development Grant for an $810,500 Warren County project with 12 jobs retained and 29 created.

IE Corp is a family-owned maker of switchgear and power infrastructure founded in 1985 and based in Price, Utah, with plants there, in South Point, Ohio and in Centralia, Illinois. ETV News reported in late 2026 that its workforce had grown from just under 300 in 2023 to about 620, which places it in the 100-499 range during the 2024-25 grant year, though it may have crossed 500 by then. JobsOhio's July 2024 report shows a $75,000 Economic Development Grant for a $12 million Lawrence County expansion with 62 jobs retained.

Westrafo America LLC is the US arm of a privately held Italian power-transformer maker whose other plants are in Vicenza, Italy and Tema, Ghana; the Trotwood plant opened in October 2025 on a $15 million initial investment. JobsOhio's October 2024 report shows a $1 million Economic Development Grant for 230 new jobs and no jobs retained, of which $71,995 was paid in FY2025. No group employee figure was published, so the bucket is inferred from three production sites and the company's statement that it has more than doubled in size since 2021.

OhioSE describes Plastic Compounders as a multi-generational family-owned recycler of post-industrial plastic that has employed local residents in Cambridge since 1965; the $25,000 Small Business Grant added an eighth extrusion line. The August 2024 JobsOhio report lists 22 jobs retained and five created on a $500,000 investment, and the Small Business Grant itself is restricted to small businesses.
